When priority inheritance was added back in 2.6.18 to sched_setscheduler()
added a path to taking an rt-mutex wait_lock
column2: which is not IRQ safe. As PI

column1: is not a common occurrence
column2: lockdep will likely never trigger if

column1: sched_setscheduler was called from interrupt context. A BUG_ON() was added
to trigger if __sched_setscheduler() was ever called from interrupt context
because there was a possibility to take the wait_lock.
Today the wait_lock is irq safe
column2: but the path to taking it in

column1: sched_setscheduler() is the same as the path to taking it from normal
context. The wait_lock is taken with raw_spin_lock_irq() and released with
raw_spin_unlock_irq() which will indiscriminately enable interrupts
which would be bad in interrupt context.
The problem is that normalize_rt_tasks
column2: which is called by triggering the

column1: sysrq nice-all-RT-tasks was changed to call __sched_setscheduler()
is done from interrupt context!
Now __sched_setscheduler() takes a ""pi"" parameter that is used to know if
the priority inheritance should be called or not. As the BUG_ON() only cares
about calling the PI code
column2: it should only bug if called from interrupt

column1: context with the ""pi"" parameter set to true.
